avoid_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Induces CYP2C9 and glucuronidation, reducing valproic acid levels and efficacy
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; consult prescriber before discontinuation to prevent breakthrough seizures

avoid_supplements.name: Carnitine (L-Carnitine supplementation)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Valproic acid impairs carnitine metabolism and increases renal losses; supplementation may be necessary but requires monitoring
avoid_supplements.action: Do not self-supplement; only use under medical supervision with carnitine level monitoring

avoid_supplements.name: High-dose Vitamin E (>400 IU daily)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: May increase bleeding risk by potentiating antiplatelet effects and hepatotoxicity
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid high-dose supplementation; maintain dietary vitamin E intake only

caution_supplements.name: Folate/Folic Acid
caution_supplements.mechanism: Valproic acid impairs folate metabolism and increases neural tube defect risk; supplementation may be beneficial
caution_supplements.action: Supplementation recommended especially in reproductive-age females; use high-dose folic acid (4-5 mg daily) as clinically indicated

caution_supplements.name: Vitamin D
caution_supplements.mechanism: Valproic acid reduces vitamin D metabolism and increases osteoporosis risk
caution_supplements.action: Monitor vitamin D levels; supplementation may be appropriate with baseline and periodic testing

caution_supplements.name: Magnesium
caution_supplements.mechanism: Valproic acid may reduce magnesium levels; magnesium may enhance therapeutic effects
caution_supplements.action: Monitor serum magnesium; supplementation may be considered if deficient

avoid_foods.name: Alcohol
avoid_foods.mechanism: Increases CNS depression, hepatotoxicity risk, and impairs valproic acid metabolism
avoid_foods.action: Completely avoid alcohol consumption during valproic acid therapy

caution_foods.name: High-fat meals
caution_foods.mechanism: May delay valproic acid absorption and reduce peak serum levels
caution_foods.action: Take valproic acid consistently with or without food; maintain consistent timing relative to meals

caution_foods.name: Cranberry juice
caution_foods.mechanism: May slightly increase urinary excretion of valproic acid through acidification
caution_foods.action: Limit intake or maintain consistent consumption; monitor seizure control if consumption changes

monitoring_notes: Monitor for hepatotoxicity, pancreatitis, and bone density loss regularly. Assess carnitine status, folate, and vitamin D levels periodically, particularly in patients at high risk (children, polypharmacy, long-term therapy). Therapeutic drug monitoring recommended to maintain levels of 50-100 mcg/mL.
